title: Factorized task x layer LoRA View code
hypothesis: A separable task-factor x layer-factor code can represent task-specific LoRA coefficients across layers with fewer serialized bytes than independent task-layer coefficients while preserving held-out function outputs. Mirror-specific value requires beating the native outer-product factorization control.
physical_object: Shared rank-4 LoRA atom basis across six layers
mirror_coordinate: Task coefficient vector and layer coefficient vector whose elementwise product yields task-layer rank coordinates
logical_multiplicity: Twelve tasks across six layers, including held-out task-layer combinations

task.metric: held-out output NRMSE, actual serialized bytes, coefficient decode MACs, CPU wall time

controls: Independent full task x layer coefficient table
Mirror task-factor x layer-factor coordinate decode
Native outer-product task/layer coefficient factorization with identical arrays and reconstruction
Task-only factor and layer-only factor lower-capacity ablations

storage.authority: Actual serialized complete inference payload bytes
paid_objects: task and layer factors or full coefficient table

success_gate: Mirror reconstruction NRMSE <=0.02 on all held-out task-layer pairs and complete bytes <=60% independent table; Mirror-specific success requires strict byte/compute/quality improvement over native outer-product factorization.
failure_gate: Quality gate miss or exact native outer-product alias without strict Pareto gain; fresh stays sealed after exact alias.
boundaries: All bases, factors, coefficients and metadata are charged
Combinatorial pair count is not independent task capacity
No natural LoRA or language model claim
